plain_english: Now who bears the adhikrti here, or how — enough to discriminate, it is said: the various grace-descent order.
sanskrit_cite: athādhikṛtibhāhanaṃ ka iha vā kathaṃ vetyalaṃ vivecayitumucyate vividhaśaktipātakramaḥ

plain_english: There some here say: grace-descent, this method — having shown that, having refuted, own view will be shown.
sanskrit_cite: tatra kecidiha prāhuḥ śaktipāta imaṃ vidhim taṃ pradarśya nirākṛtya svamataṃ darśayiṣyate

plain_english: There this seen, existent-pleasure-pain-deluded, unequal — existing become thus; posit an equal cause.
sanskrit_cite: tatredaṃ dṛśyamānaṃ satsukhaduḥkhavimohabhāk viṣamaṃ sattathābhūtaṃ samaṃ hetuṃ prakalpayet

plain_english: That manifest, insentient various-formed from sattva and the rest — like pot and the rest, an effect, thus; its one cause — that night.
sanskrit_cite: so@vyaktaṃ tacca sattvādinānārūpamacetanam ghaṭādivatkāryamiti hetureko@sya sā niśā

plain_english: That inert, effect-formed, effect in her with God indeed — kala-to-earth-ended; from inertia she is unfit for creation.
sanskrit_cite: sā jaḍā kāryatādrūpyātkāryaṃ cāsyāṃ sadeva hi kalādidharaṇīprāntaṃ jāḍyātsā sūtaye@kṣamā

plain_english: By him the Lord would agitate her; her agitation is birth-fitness — toward man, and she produces enjoyable sounds, various kinds.
sanskrit_cite: teneśaḥ kṣobhayedenāṃ kṣobho@syāḥ sūtiyogyatā puṃsaḥ prati ca sā bhogyaṃ sūte@nādīn pṛthagvidhān

plain_english: Of person in non-distinctness, toward liberated souls, why not that cause? Karma-impression — and it in them is not found.
sanskrit_cite: puṃsaśca nirviśeṣatve muktāṇūn prati kiṃ na tat nimittaṃ karmasaṃskāraḥ sa ca teṣu na vidyate

plain_english: Thus if their karma-impression-absence — whence indeed? Not from enjoyment-other-karma-portion involvement, for hard to cross.
sanskrit_cite: iti cetkarmasaṃskārābhāvasteṣāṃ kutaḥ kila na bhogādanyakarmāṃśaprasaṅgo hi duratyayaḥ

plain_english: Simultaneous actions' enjoyment is not fitting; by sequence indeed — of which action the fruit? Therefore why would own form sometimes abandon?
sanskrit_cite: yugapatkarmaṇāṃ bhogo naca yuktaḥ krameṇa hi phaledyatkarma tatkasmātsvaṃ rūpaṃ saṃtyajetkvacit

plain_english: From knowledge karma-destruction, if that — how? From Lord-impulsion, from dharma, if — how? He too — from karma, if that, let it be said.
sanskrit_cite: jñānātkarmakṣayaścettatkuta īśvaracoditāt dharmādyadi kutaḥ so@pi karmataścettaducyatām

plain_english: No karma is such that knowledge arises by it — and karma-born, that knowledge in fruit-heap falls certainly.
sanskrit_cite: nahi karmāsti tādṛkṣaṃ yena jñānaṃ pravartate karmajatve ca tajjñānaṃ phalarāśau pateddhruvam

plain_english: Other-karma fruit, former karma-mass — what would burn? Of the Lord, even devoid of hatred-attachment, how ever?
sanskrit_cite: anyakarmaphalaṃ prācyaṃ karmarāśiṃ ca kiṃ dahet īśasya dveṣarāgādiśūnyasyāpi kathaṃ kvacit

plain_english: Thus intention, not elsewhere, from absence of difference-cause — but thus knowledge would burn karma-nets; karma indeed.
sanskrit_cite: tathābhisaṃdhirnānyatra bhedahetorabhāvataḥ nanvitthaṃ pradahejjñānaṃ karmajālāni karma hi

plain_english: Ignorance-cooperating this produces heaven-and-rest fruit — ignorance from knowledge perishes, also from other-karma fruit.
sanskrit_cite: ajñānasahakārīdaṃ sūte svargādikaṃ phalam ajñānaṃ jñānato naśyedanyakarmaphalādapi

plain_english: Fasting and the rest, and other evil-karma fruit may be — renders fruitless the evil, accepted as karma indeed.
sanskrit_cite: upavāsādikaṃ cānyadduṣṭakarmaphalaṃ bhavet niṣphalīkurute duṣṭaṃ karmetyaṅgīkṛtaṃ kila

plain_english: Ignorance thus, what is said: if knowledge-absence — what then? Prior absence or destruction; in the first, what of all cognitions?
sanskrit_cite: ajñānamiti yatproktaṃ jñānābhāvaḥ sa cetsa kim prāgabhāvo@thavā dhvaṃsa ādye kiṃ sarvasaṃvidām

plain_english: Of anyone, or then, knowledge — the eastern thesis is impossible: not one whose knowledge arose such-like.
sanskrit_cite: kasyāpi vātha jñānasya prācyaḥ pakṣastvasaṃbhavī na kiṃcidyasya vijñānamudapādi tathāvidhaḥ

plain_english: Not even an atom exists in existence, indeed in this beginningless — what now this order? Of future, prior-absence of knowledge, established being.
sanskrit_cite: nāṇurasti bhave hyasminnanādau ko@nvayaṃ kramaḥ bhāvinaḥ prāgabhāvaśca jñānasyeti sthite sati

plain_english: Of the liberated atom too, he is indeed from birth; before, this one — and not knowledge future, when liberated in this — if discussed, this.
sanskrit_cite: muktāṇorapi so@styeva janmataḥ prāgasau naca jñānaṃ bhāvi vimukte@sminniti ceccarcyatāmidam

plain_english: Why knowledge not to be here — indeed from body-and-rest birth? Therefore why from karma depletion — whence knowledge-loss?
sanskrit_cite: kasmājjñānaṃ na bhāvyatra nanu dehādyajanmataḥ tatkasmātkarmaṇaḥ kṣaiṇyāttatkuto@jñānahānitaḥ

plain_english: Of ignorance, how loss — in prior absence indeed of consciousness? Ignorance is that prior absence — not, from impossibility of future production.
sanskrit_cite: ajñānasya kathaṃ hāniḥ prāgabhāve hi saṃvidaḥ ajñānaṃ prāgabhāvo@sau na bhāvyutpattyasaṃbhavāt

plain_english: Why not future that knowledge — indeed from body-and-rest birth? Thus this all-party-destroyer, sharp-wheel whirling.
sanskrit_cite: kasmānna bhāvi tajjñānaṃ nanu dehādyajanmataḥ ityeṣa sarvapakṣaghno niśitaścakrakabhramaḥ

plain_english: Now destruction indeed is this ignorance, situated always — in liberated atoms thus; in them let Maya-effect expansion be.
sanskrit_cite: atha pradhvaṃsa evedamajñānaṃ tatsadā sthitam muktāṇuṣviti teṣvastu māyākāryavijṛmbhitam

plain_english: Now ignorance is not non-existence but false knowledge — their view; that very, of actions in own duty, is co-cause.
sanskrit_cite: athājñānaṃ nahyabhāvo mithyājñānaṃ tu tanmatam tadeva karmaṇāṃ svasminkartavye sahakāraṇam

plain_english: What action should be declared, when it produces its own fruit, if causality is obtained only through false knowledge?
sanskrit_cite: vaktavyaṃ tarhi kiṃ karma yadā sūte svakaṃ phalam tadaiva mithyājñānena satā hetutvamāpyate

plain_english: Now, if false knowledge is truly present at the moment action is performed, what fruit comes from such action?
sanskrit_cite: atha yasminkṣaṇe karma kṛtaṃ tatra svarūpasat mithyājñānaṃ yadi tatastādṛśātkamarṇaḥ phalam

plain_english: In the prior view, after dissolution and at the beginning of creation, false knowledge has no possibility anywhere because body and the rest are absent.
sanskrit_cite: prākpakṣe pralaye vṛtte prācyasṛṣṭipravartane dehādyabhāvānno mithyājñānasya kvāpi saṃbhavaḥ

plain_english: In the latter view, whenever and wherever action is done, all of it is accompanied by ignorance.
sanskrit_cite: uttarasminpunaḥ pakṣe yadā yadyena yatra vā kriyate karma tatsarvamajñānasacivaṃ tadā

plain_english: Necessarily, for anyone, destruction of karma would not occur, even if, having become a knower, one performs some action.
sanskrit_cite: avaśyamiti kasyāpi na karmaprakṣayo bhavet yadyapi jñānavānbhūtvā vidhatte karma kiṃcana

plain_english: Action would be fruitless, but what course remains for the prior mass of karma, even at dissolution, through union with conscious nature?
sanskrit_cite: viphalaṃ syāttu tatpūrvakarmarāśau tu kā gatiḥ atha pralayakāle @pi citsvabhāvatvayogataḥ

plain_english: Knowledge arises indeed from atoms as false; whence from nature? Not so in liberated Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: aṇūnā saṃbhavatyeva jñānaṃ mithyeti tatkutaḥ svabhāvāditi cenmukte śive vā kiṃ tathā nahi

plain_english: That which is called non-seeing is the cause in transforming primal matter, indeed from the mixture of both distinctnesses.
sanskrit_cite: yaccādarśanamākhyātaṃ nimittaṃ pariṇāmini pradhāne taddhi saṃkīrṇavaivittayobhayayogataḥ

plain_english: For seeing, beginning with intellect accompanied by fitness for human aim, up to earth, there is whatever arises from mind.
sanskrit_cite: darśanāya pumarthaikayogyatāsacivaṃ dhiyaḥ ārabhya sate dharaṇīparyantaṃ tatra yaccitaḥ

plain_english: Experience, called that, is non-distinction of intellect function, from grace of personal effort and manifestation of intellect with object.
sanskrit_cite: buddhivṛttyaviśiṣṭatvaṃ puṃsprayāśarprasādataḥ prakāśanāddhiyo@rthena saha bhogaḥ sa bhaṇyate

plain_english: Intellect itself I am; but another having modification nature, different from me, is indeed in whose consciousness?
sanskrit_cite: buddhirevāsmi vikṛtidharmikānyastu ko@pyasau madvilakṣaṇa ekātmetyevaṃ vaivi yasaṃvidi

plain_english: Because human aim is accomplished and the cooperator is separated, it does not produce toward that person, but indeed another.
sanskrit_cite: pumarthasya kṛtatvena sahakāriviyogataḥ taṃ pumāṃsaṃ prati naiva sūte kiṃtvanyameva hi

plain_english: Here, the root nature of a person is seeing, or one of two; let this alternative be spoken.
sanskrit_cite: atra puṃso@tha mūlasya dharmo@darśanatā dvayoḥ athaveti vikalpo@yamāstāmetattu bhaṇyatām

plain_english: Experience extends up to discrimination; there, what is the limit if all is seen? That too, what?
sanskrit_cite: bhogo vivekaparyanta iti yattatra ko@vadhiḥ vivekalābhe nikhilasūtidṛgyadi sāpi kim

plain_english: Generally or by particulars, in the prior view it would be from one birth; in the latter view, never, by union of future time.
sanskrit_cite: sāmānyena viśeṣairvā prācye syādekajanmataḥ uttare na kadācitsyādbhāvikālasya yogataḥ

plain_english: If by some particulars all become simultaneous, discrimination from beginningless union would leave what mutual variety?
sanskrit_cite: kaiścideva viśeṣaiścetsarveṣāṃ yugapadbhavet viveko@nādisaṃyogātkā hyanyonyaṃ vicitratā

plain_english: Therefore, even by Samkhya view, this ignorance is not fitted; without ignorance, bondage and liberation have no order.
sanskrit_cite: tasmātsāṃkhyadṛśāpīdamajñānaṃ naiva yujyate ajñānena vinā bandhamokṣau naiva vyavasthayā

plain_english: They are fitted, but that is not established by stated reasons, even if fear, action, and gods' will exist.
sanskrit_cite: yujyete tacca kathitayuktibhirnopapadyate bhāyākarmāṇudevecchāsadbhāve@pi sthite tataḥ

plain_english: There is no union of bondage and liberation because a difference cause is impossible; therefore by the word ignorance, knowership and agency natures are meant.
sanskrit_cite: na bandhamokṣayoryogo bhedahetorasaṃbhavāt tasmādajñānaśabdena jñatvakartṛtvadharmaṇām

plain_english: The covering of conscious atoms is something to be spoken by the wise, established as covering nature, non-different from its own form.
sanskrit_cite: cidaṇūnāmāvaraṇaṃ kiṃcidvācyaṃ vipaścitā āvāraṇātmanā siddhaṃ tatsvarūpādabhedavat

plain_english: In difference and absence of proof, that one in all selves; whence is it produced? If from maya, how indeed is that?
sanskrit_cite: bhede pramāṇābhāvācca tadekaṃ nikhilātmasu tacca kasmātprasūtaṃ syānmāyātaścetkathaṃ nu sā

plain_english: Somewhere only, well-traversed not this; in liberated self thus this prior further question: would a cause be obtained if not?
sanskrit_cite: kvacideva suvītaitanna tu muktātmanītyayam prācyaḥ paryanuyogaḥ syānnimittaṃ cenna labhyate

plain_english: From absence of origination by that, it is eternal and does not perish; from that, in oneness only, and from commonality of other self.
sanskrit_cite: utpattyabhāvatastena nityaṃ naca vinaśyati tata evaikatāyāṃ cānyātmasādhāraṇatvataḥ

plain_english: Not from being cause of a real thing, not from concealment of mind, and not union of selves by this self, because of its impossibility.
sanskrit_cite: na vāvastvarthakāritvānna cittatsaṃvṛtitvataḥ na caitenātmanāṃ yogo hetumāṃstadasaṃbhavāt

plain_english: Therefore one thing, always bound with selves, inert impurity, that ignorance, is the cause of samsara's sprout.
sanskrit_cite: tenaikaṃ vastu sannityaṃ nityasaṃbaddhamātmabhiḥ jaḍaṃ malaṃ tadajñānaṃ saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇam

plain_english: When its obstructing power rests, by Shiva's rays the soul is touched, and its own knowledge and action become clear.
sanskrit_cite: tasya roddhrī yadā śaktirudāste śivaraśmibhiḥ tadāṇuḥ spṛśyate spṛṣṭaḥ svake jñānakriye sphuṭe

plain_english: This soul enters, like a sunstone by a ray, impelled, through the graded mediation of the obstructing power.
sanskrit_cite: samāviśedayaṃ sūryakānto@rkeṇeva coditaḥ roddhryāśca śaktermādhyasthyatāratamyavaśakramāat

plain_english: Therefore they call variety in manifestation of self-awareness; this is defined in scriptures as descent of power.
sanskrit_cite: vicitratvamataḥ prāhurabhivyaktau svasaṃvidaḥ sa eṣa śaktipātākhyaḥ śāstreṣu paribhāṣyate

plain_english: Here it is said that impurity thus is not fitting; what fruit is there in repeating what was stated earlier?
sanskrit_cite: atrocyate malastāvaditthameṣa na yujyate iti pūrvāhṇike proktaṃ punaruktau tu kiṃ phalam

plain_english: What is the ripening of impurity? If destruction of other selves, then calling that one impurity attaches purity.
sanskrit_cite: malasya pākaḥ ko @yaṃ syānnāśaśceditarātmanām sa eko mala ityukternairmalyamanuṣajyate

plain_english: Now impurity, per soul and beginningless like prior absence, would perish; yet this destruction must be caused.
sanskrit_cite: atha pratyātmaniyato@nādiśca prāgabhāvavat malo naśyettathāpyeṣa nāśo yadi sahetukaḥ

plain_english: The cause is karma or the lord's will; karma is not such, and the lord's free will is only sometimes; so what then?
sanskrit_cite: hetuḥ karmeśvarecchā vā karma tāvanna tādṛśam īśvarecchā svatantrā ca kvacideva tathaiva kim

plain_english: If its destruction is uncaused, then it already perishes; after a moment similar production follows; if so, only steadiness remains.
sanskrit_cite: ahetuko@sya nāśaścetprāgevaiṣa vinaśyatu kṣaṇāntaraṃ sadṛk sūte iti cetsthirataiva sā

plain_english: Destruction is not seen for eternal being whose birth is not cause-dependent; prior absence is nonexistent, so be it.
sanskrit_cite: na ca nityasya bhāvasya hetvanāyattajanmanaḥ nāśo dṛṣṭaḥ prāgabhāvastvavastviti tathāstu saḥ

plain_english: Now its ripening is named boundness to own power toward all; so it would be obstructed power, like poison-fire.
sanskrit_cite: athāsya pāko nāmaiṣa svaśaktipratibaddhatā sarvānprati tathaiṣa syādruddhaśaktirviṣāgnivat

plain_english: If power arises again, its own effect would arise like poison-fire; even liberated ones would not be liberated; we do not accept its power.
sanskrit_cite: punarudbhūtaśaktau ca svakāryaṃ syādviṣāgnivat muktā api na muktāḥ syuḥ śaktiṃ cāsya na manmahe

plain_english: If obstruction is mere existence of knowledge and agency, then possibility of Shiva-liberated soul is compromised.
sanskrit_cite: roddhrīti cetkasya nṛṇāṃ jñatvakartṛtvayoryadi sadbhāvamātrādroddhṛtve śivamuktāṇvasaṃbhavaḥ

plain_english: Impurity does nothing beyond proximity; by itself changeability would imply impermanence.
sanskrit_cite: saṃnidhānātiriktaṃ ca na kiṃcitkurute malaḥ ātmanā pariṇāmitvādanityatvaprasaṅgataḥ

plain_english: Souls are not dependent on knowledge and agency only; if that is obstructed, alas, destruction of form follows.
sanskrit_cite: jñatvakartṛtvamātraṃ ca pudgalā na tadāśrayāḥ taccedāvāritaṃ hanta rūpanāśaḥ prasajyate

plain_english: Covering is invisibility, and it does not make otherness of that thing; knowledge like a pot cannot be covered.
sanskrit_cite: āvāraṇaṃ cādṛśyatvaṃ na ca tadvastuno@nyatām karoti ghaṭavajjñānaṃ nāvarītuṃ ca śakyate

plain_english: How is that same covering not known by coverable knowledge? Otherwise covering would be name only.
sanskrit_cite: jñānenāvaraṇīyena tadevāvaraṇaṃ katham na jñāyate tathā ca syādāvṛtirnāmamātrataḥ

plain_english: Who is the obstacle to the obstructing power? The lord; if without dependence, the previously given answer applies.
sanskrit_cite: roddhryāśca śakteḥ kastasya pratibandhaka īśvaraḥ yadyapekṣāvirahitastatra prāgdattamuttaram

plain_english: Considering equality of karma, its will proceeds; its form must be stated; what equality of karmas indeed?
sanskrit_cite: karmasāmyamapekṣyātha tasyecchā saṃpravartate tasyāpi rūpaṃ vaktavyaṃ samatā karmaṇāṃ hi kā

plain_english: By greatness of enjoyment cycle in time, toward some fruit, from opposition karmas obstructed and standing, such equality arises.
sanskrit_cite: bhogaparyāyamāhātmyātkāle kvāpi phalaṃ prati virodhātkarmaṇī ruddhe tiṣṭhataḥ sāmyamīdṛśam

plain_english: The all-knowing god, having seen that time-portion, obstructs that impurity; that time is marked by avoiding pleasure, pain, and so on.
sanskrit_cite: taṃ ca kālāṃśakaṃ devaḥ sarvajño vīkṣya taṃ malam runddhe lakṣyaḥ sa kālaśca sukhaduḥkhādivarjanaiḥ

plain_english: Not by sequential pure or mixed form karmas; so too in own fruit to be given, what is this mutual obstruction?
sanskrit_cite: naitatkramikasaṃśuddhavyāmiśrākārakarmabhiḥ tathaiva deye svaphale keyamanyonyaroddhṛtā

plain_english: If both are obstructed, birth and lifespan would not be; therefore the body would fall; if cessation is only of enjoyments, indeed?
sanskrit_cite: rodhe tayośca jātyāyurapi na syādataḥ patet deho bhogadayoreva nirodha iti cennanu

plain_english: If Shankara obstructs impurity in presence of karma giving birth and lifespan, what does he fear from enjoyment-giving karma?
sanskrit_cite: jātyāyuṣpradakarmāṃśasaṃnidhau yadi śaṃkaraḥ malaṃ runddhe bhogadātuḥ karmaṇaḥ kiṃ bibheti saḥ

plain_english: Even gathering hundreds of states free from heat and cold, devotion-rasa immersion is not seen in abundance.
sanskrit_cite: śataśo@pi hlādatāpaśūnyāṃ saṃcinvate daśām na ca bhaktirasāveśamiti bhūmnā vilokitam

plain_english: Even so, considering the greatness of time, the supreme lord acts thus; what kind is that time?
sanskrit_cite: athāpi kālamāhātmyamapekṣya parameśvaraḥ tathā karoti vaktavyaṃ kālo@sau kīdṛśastviti

plain_english: What of this beginningless enjoyment and beginningless karma with person? Hence enjoyment-cycle time is unequalled for all.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ cānādirayaṃ bhogaḥ karmānādi sapudgalam tataśca bhogaparyāyakālaḥ sarvasya niḥsamaḥ

plain_english: If there were a beginning for someone, variety would arise from that class; enjoyed by this and by this aeon, but the pair.
sanskrit_cite: ādimattve hi kasyāpi vargādasmādbhavediyam vaicitrī bhuktametena kalpametena tu dvayam

plain_english: From so much enjoyment cycle there would be equality of karmas; by this method-seed I think the cause of variety.
sanskrit_cite: iyato bhogaparyāyātsyātsāmyaṃ karmaṇāmiti anena nayabījena manye vaicitryakāraṇam

plain_english: The world's fixed karma does not fit thus; atoms covered by beginningless impurity are cognition-action-self.
sanskrit_cite: jagataḥ karma yatklaptaṃ tattathā nāvakalpate anādimalasaṃcchannā aṇavo dṛkkriyātmanā

plain_english: How are all equal yet resort to variegated karma succession by enjoyment craving? Variegated indeed, whence?
sanskrit_cite: sarve tulyāḥ kathaṃ citrāṃ śritāḥ karmaparamparām bhogalolikayā cetsā vicitreti kuto nanu

plain_english: If again beginningless karma impression variety is to be said, that same variety, whence of necessity and attachment?
sanskrit_cite: anādi karmasaṃskāravaicitryāditi cetpunaḥ vācyaṃ tadeva vaicitryaṃ kuto niyatirāgayoḥ

plain_english: If this greatness, why are those two not inconsistent sharers? But independence from lord's will is not a possible cause of difference.
sanskrit_cite: mahimā cedayaṃ tau kiṃ nāsamañjasyabhāginau īśvarecchānapekṣā tu bhedaheturna kalpate

plain_english: By beginninglessness alone, reasonless, impurity of order is proved; then let it be by impurity, vain by this.
sanskrit_cite: athānāditvamātreṇa yuktihīnena sādhyate vyavastheyamalaṃ tarhi malenāstu vṛthāmunā

plain_english: For thus karma lasts not until maya is active in person; and cause, its course, that measured impurity.
sanskrit_cite: tathāhi karma tāvanno yāvanmāyā na pudgale vyāpriyeta na cāhetustadvṛttistanmito malaḥ

plain_english: Thus and in assumed maya-effect in karma, causality; if beginningless karma goes, what of assumption of impurity?
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ ca kalpite māyākārye karmaṇi hetutām anādi karma cedgacchetkiṃ malasyopakalpanam

plain_english: Surely may there be no impurity then — in variegated forms, in continuously revolving acts, order is not established.
sanskrit_cite: nanu mābhūnmalastarhi citrākāreṣu karmasu santatyāvartamāneṣu vyavasthā na prakalpate

plain_english: At first, in the middle, from action-variety — not as equal; even self-form, some this, in future time would be so.
sanskrit_cite: ādau madhye ca citratvātkarmaṇāṃ na yathā samaḥ ātmākāro@pi ko@pyeṣa bhāvikāle tathā bhavet

plain_english: Thus cut off indeed is this bondage-liberation-etc. course — bondage from ignorance, liberation from knowledge, thus examined.
sanskrit_cite: itthamucchinna evāyaṃ bandhamokṣādikaḥ kramaḥ ajñānādbandhanaṃ mokṣo jñānāditi parīkṣitam

plain_english: In opposition, self-fruited, these two karmas, at some time — if neutralized, then let this karma be awakened.
sanskrit_cite: virodhe svaphale caite karmaṇī samaye kvacit udāsāte yadi tataḥ karmaitatpratibudhyatām

plain_english: Of Shiva-power descent, what room, by that much — somewhere, at a time, when of those two this indifference, then?
sanskrit_cite: śivaśaktinipātasya ko@vakāśastu tāvatā kvāpi kāle tayoretadaudāsīnyaṃ yadā tataḥ

plain_english: In another time, from non-cessation of such opposition — and therefore at fruit-end not, by those two, and other karmas.
sanskrit_cite: kālāntare tayostadvadvirodhasyānivṛttitaḥ ataśca na phaletānte tābhyāṃ karmāntaraṇi ca

plain_english: Blocked, attained-time, by the two enjoyable — thus always in report, at body-fall likewise.
sanskrit_cite: ruddhāni prāptakālatvādgatābhyāmupabhogyatām evaṃ sadaiva vārtāyāṃ dehapāte tathaiva ca

plain_english: When born, liberation — so be it; grace-descent-etc. supposition — then at indifference-two-karma-union moment.
sanskrit_cite: jāte vimokṣa ityāstāṃ śaktipātādikalpanā athodāsīnatatkarmadvayayogakṣaṇāntare

plain_english: Another karma fruits, even at that moment, likewise — what not? In another moment then, they indeed, free from obstruction.
sanskrit_cite: karmāntaraṃ phalaṃ sūte tatkṣaṇe@pi tathā na kim kṣaṇāntare@tha te eva pratibandhavivarjite

plain_english: From fruit, obstruction's removal — what done? Of those two, karma-equality by own nature, not; and having gradation.
sanskrit_cite: phalataḥ pratibandhasya varjanaṃ kiṃkṛtaṃ tayoḥ karmasāmyaṃ svarūpeṇa na ca tattāratamyabhāk

plain_english: Not 'Shiva wills thus' — in that act, in grace-descent, that would not happen; and concealment named this — why would he arise again?
sanskrit_cite: na śiveccheti tatkārye śaktipāte na tadbhavet tirobhāvaśca nāmāyaṃ sa kasmādudbhavetpunaḥ

plain_english: By karma-equality, what is to be done was already done before indeed — in causality, and by Shiva-will to be said, just as before.
sanskrit_cite: karmasāmyena yatkṛtyaṃ prāgevaitatkṛtaṃ kila hetutve ceśvarecchāyā vācyaṃ pūrvavadeva tu

plain_english: By this, others too, to be examined, posited in Lord's will — they too are destroyed, from eternal-causeless-beginning refutation.
sanskrit_cite: etenānye@pi ye@pekṣyā īśecchāyāṃ prakalpitāḥ dhvastāste@pi hi nityānyahetvahetvādidūṣaṇāt

plain_english: Dispassion, enjoyment-aversion, some duty, discrimination — good company, constant supreme-Lord worship-practice.
sanskrit_cite: vairāgyaṃ bhogavairasyaṃ dharmaḥ ko@pi vivekitā satsaṅgaḥ parameśānapūjādyabhyāsanityatā

plain_english: Calamity-arrival watching, in body some mark — scripture-service, enjoyment-group fullness, lordly knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: āpatprāptistannirīkṣā dehe kiṃcicca lakṣaṇam śāstrasevā bhogasaṃghapūrṇatā jñānamaiśvaram

plain_english: Thus considered, if of the Lord — and this refutable, as before; and deviation by universality-particularity, from own nature.
sanskrit_cite: ityapekṣyaṃ yadīśasya dūṣyametacca pūrvavat vyabhicāraśca sāmastyavyastatvābhyāṃ svarūpataḥ

plain_english: Mutual non-entry and impossibility, the more — therefore we do not think: who is this, of grace-descent order, the order?
sanskrit_cite: anyonyānupraveśaścānupapattiśca bhūyasī tasmānna manmahe ko@yaṃ śaktipātavidheḥ kramaḥ

plain_english: Thus delusion-poison-entering-swoon-release-giving, Sri-Shambhu-mouth-uttered — I speak the agama great medicine.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ bhrāntiviṣāveśamūrcchānirmokadāyinīm śrīśaṃbhuvadanodgīrṇāṃ vacmyāgamamahauṣadhīm

plain_english: Lord, free consciousness-formed, light-self, by nature — by form-concealment-play-yoga, atomic, manifold.
sanskrit_cite: devaḥ svatantraścidrūpaḥ prakāśātmā svabhāvataḥ rūpapracchādanakrīḍāyogādaṇuranekakaḥ

plain_english: He himself, by imagined-form-conceptual acts, binds himself here indeed — from freedom, so described.
sanskrit_cite: sa svayaṃ kalpitākāravikalpātmakakarmabhiḥ badhnātyātmānameveha svātantryāditi varṇitam

plain_english: Freedom-greatness indeed this of the Lord, because that one again — own thoroughly-pure form, touching reality though atomic.
sanskrit_cite: svātantryamahimaivāyaṃ devasya yadasau punaḥ svaṃ rūpaṃ pariśuddhaṃ satspṛśatyapyaṇutāmayaḥ

plain_english: Not to be said, but how, named, in some man thus — not indeed a name, some man in whom questioned.
sanskrit_cite: na vācyaṃ tu kathaṃ nāma kasmiṃścitpuṃsyasau tathā nahi nāma pumānkaścidyasminparyanuyujyate

plain_english: God indeed, so that one, if his own form such — of such-manifestation nature, in nature what suitability?
sanskrit_cite: deva eva tathāsau cet svarūpaṃ cāsya tādṛśam tādṛkprathāsvabhāvasya svabhāve kānuyojyatā

plain_english: Says our supreme lord, and in Shiva-view, the supreme teacher — five-kinds-action-statement Shiva-nature for own action.
sanskrit_cite: āhāsmatparameṣṭhī ca śivadṛṣṭau gurūttamaḥ pañcaprakārakṛtyoktiśivatvānnijakarmaṇe

plain_english: Of the proceeded, other causes — where seeking? In concealed-true-nature appearance, in person, whatever fruit.
sanskrit_cite: pravṛttasya nimittānāmapareṣāṃ kva mārgaṇam channasvarūpatābhāse puṃsi yadyādṛśaṃ phalam

plain_english: There, of the existing atom, freedom indeed is, from karma — that, and the Lord's which self-conceal-wish, causality.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāṇoḥ sata evāsti svātantryaṃ karmatohi tat īśvarasya ca yā svātmatirodhitsā nimittatām

plain_english: It approaches: karma-mala-hence-non-divine-establishment; concealment is full-form's incompleteness, and that is filling.
sanskrit_cite: sābhyeti karmamalayorato@nādivyavasthitiḥ tirodhiḥ pūrṇarūpasyāpūrṇatvaṃ tacca pūraṇam

plain_english: Towards, by distinct state, desired — foolish impurity, without pure-self-luminous-self Shiva-nature.
sanskrit_cite: prati bhinnena bhāvena spṛhāto lolikā malaḥ viśuddhasvaprakāśātmaśivarūpatayā vinā

plain_english: Not anything is joined by that; cause here is the great Lord — thus in creation-preservation-destruction triad he depends on Maya.
sanskrit_cite: na kiṃcidyujyate tena heturatra maheśvaraḥ itthaṃ sṛṣṭisthitidhvaṃsatraye māyāmapekṣate

plain_english: For action, impurity and karma, as Shiva-will alone — well established; but in whatever Shiva by own form shines.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtyai malaṃ tathā karma śivecchaiveti susthitam yattu kasmiṃścana śivaḥ svena rūpeṇa bhāsate

plain_english: There his, not in atom, so-long dependent — mala and karma, in atomic-nature loss, gone-into-that, causality — how?
sanskrit_cite: tatrāsya nāṇuge tāvadapekṣye malakarmaṇī aṇusvarūpatāhānau tadgataṃ hetutāṃ katham

plain_english: Go Maya-independence — therefore establish thus; thereby pure self-luminous Shiva indeed here is cause.
sanskrit_cite: vrajenmāyānapekṣatvamata evopapādayet tena śuddhaḥ svaprakāśaḥ śiva evātra kāraṇam

plain_english: He, by mere free will, gradation-revealer — clan-birth-body-action-age-observance abundance.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca svācchandyamātreṇa tāratamyaprakāśakaḥ kulajātivapuṣkarmavayonuṣṭhānasaṃpadaḥ

plain_english: Regardless, in Shiva devotion — grace-descent of fruit-seekers; which by fruit-desire, devotion depends on karma and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: anapekṣya śive bhaktiḥ śaktipāto@phalārthinām yā phalārthitayā bhaktiḥ sā karmādyamapekṣate

plain_english: Then there would be in fruit difference, not in liberation — but that one thus, of the both-enjoyment-liberation aimer also, clearly.
sanskrit_cite: tato@tra syātphale bhedo nāpavarge tvasau tathā bhogāpavargadvitayābhisaṃdhāturapi sphuṭam

plain_english: In prior part looks karma, from wonder, not later, again — even unilluminated form, by that illumination only, that.
sanskrit_cite: prāgbhāge@pekṣate karma citratvānnottare punaḥ anābhāsitarūpo@pi tadābhāsitayeva yat

plain_english: Having stood and gathered mantra and so forth, he would abandon his concealment; the blessed one declared this in the Sri Sara Shastra.
sanskrit_cite: sthitvā mantrādi saṃgṛhya tyajetso@sya tirobhavaḥ śrīsāraśāstre bhagavānvastvetatsamabhāṣata

plain_english: He wraps himself, without doubt, in many states made of dharma and adharma, from avicya to the end of shiva.
sanskrit_cite: dharmādharmātmakairbhāvairanekairveṣṭayetsvayam asandehaṃ svamātmānamavīcyādiśivāntake

plain_english: By a group of powers like that, he indeed wraps himself; the lord of gods binds and also releases himself.
sanskrit_cite: tadvacchaktisamūhena sa eva tu viveṣṭayet svayaṃ badhnāti deveśaḥ svayaṃ caiva vimuñcati

plain_english: He himself is enjoyer, knower, and marker; enjoyment and liberation are himself; the goddess and lord are himself.
sanskrit_cite: svayaṃ bhoktā svayaṃ jñātā svayaṃ caivopalakṣayet svayaṃ bhuktiśca muktiśca svayaṃ devī svayaṃ prabhuḥ

plain_english: He himself is the one syllable; as heat of the black path, the thing spoken here is manifestation of self-form by freedom.
sanskrit_cite: svayamekākṣarā caiva yathoṣmā kṛṣṇavartmanaḥ vastūktamatra svātantryātsvātmarūpaprakāśanam

plain_english: In Sri Nishakula it is also said: small-minded ones with falsely imagined minds suffer by examining impurity and illusion.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmanniśākule@pyuktaṃ mithyābhāvitacetasaḥ malamāyāvicāreṇa kliśyante svalpabuddhayaḥ

plain_english: Dear one, what can dust do to crystal? As blue in the sky, abandon suspicion of impurity from that.
sanskrit_cite: sphaṭikopalago reṇuḥ kiṃ tasya kurutāṃ priye vyomnīva nīlaṃ hi malaṃ malaśaṃkāṃ tatastyajet

plain_english: The glorious knowledge teacher said: in view of proof and praise, at the time of destruction of dharma-adharma pervasion, descent of power is accepted by those who conceal.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmānvidyāguruścāha pramāṇastutidarśane dharmādharmavyāptivināśāntarakāle śakteḥ pāto gāhanikairyaḥ pratipannaḥ

plain_english: Agreeing by own will, hymns and so forth would declare freedom independent of principles; gradation manifests as intense, moderate, and mild.
sanskrit_cite: taṃ svecchātaḥ saṃgiramāṇāḥ stavakādyāḥ svātantryaṃ tattvayyanapekṣaṃ kathayeyuḥ tāratamyaprakāśo yastīvramadhyamamandatāḥ

plain_english: Those indeed are each of descent of power, established in threefold; intense-intense descent of power occurs by fall of body itself.
sanskrit_cite: tā eva śaktipātasya pratyekaṃ traidhamāsthitāḥ tīvratīvraḥ śaktipāto dehapātavaśātsvayam

plain_english: Liberation-giving at that time or other; by gradation, from moderate-intense again all ignorance turns away.
sanskrit_cite: mokṣapradastadaivānyakāle vā tāratamyataḥ madhyatīvrātpunaḥ sarvamajñānaṃ vinivartate

plain_english: Because he himself knows selfhood as bondage and liberation, that intuitive great knowledge is independent of scripture and teacher.
sanskrit_cite: svayameva yato vetti bandhamokṣatayātmatām tatprātibhaṃ mahājñānaṃ śāstrācāryānapekṣi yat.

plain_english: Intuition-moonlight quiets darkness, and the teacher-moon destroys darkness and heat, opening bliss-filled sight.
sanskrit_cite: pratibhācandrikāśāntadhvāntaścācāryacandramāḥ tamastāpau hanti dṛśaṃ visphāryānandanirbharām

plain_english: He is disciple from doership; another is disciple from action-state; everywhere in smarta status, time, family, and so forth.
sanskrit_cite: sa śiṣṭaḥ karmakartṛtvācchiṣyo@nyaḥ karmabhāvataḥ śiṣṭaḥ sarvatra ca smārtapadakālakulādiṣu

plain_english: The self-born, established in scripture meaning and intuition, is said; by that rooted instruction no creature is empty.
sanskrit_cite: uktaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ śāstrārthapratibhāpariniṣṭhitaḥ yanmūlaṃ śāsanaṃ tena na riktaḥ ko@pi jantukaḥ

plain_english: Even there, gradation-born infinity; firmness awaits reasoning, scripture, teacher speech, practice, and so forth.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi tāratamyotthamānantyaṃ dārḍhyakamprate yuktiḥ śāstraṃ gururvādo@bhyāsa ityādyapekṣate

plain_english: Shaking knowledge indeed returns again itself; firmness of another comes by reasoning and so forth by others alone.
sanskrit_cite: kampamānaṃ hi vijñānaṃ svayameva punarvrajet kasyāpi dārḍhyamanyasya yuktyādyaiḥ kevaletaraiḥ

plain_english: As less dependence on others may be in intuition, so that teacher is best, gone beyond knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: yathā yathā parāpekṣātānavaṃ prātibhe bhavet tathā tathā gururasau śreṣṭho vijñānapāragaḥ

plain_english: Even learned infinite knowledge from elsewhere; by power of intuition, what he knows there, that shivahood is greater.
sanskrit_cite: anyataḥ śikṣitānantajñāno@pi pratibhābalāt yadvetti tatra tatrāsya śivatā jyāyasī ca sā

plain_english: For him, order of initiation and so forth is not, nor consecration, nor lineage and so forth, nor vow of knowledge on the intuitive path.
sanskrit_cite: na cāsya samayitvādikramo nāpyabhiṣecanam na santānādi no vidyāvrataṃ prātibhavartmanaḥ

plain_english: The primordial knower great god is established by that; because purifications are for establishment accomplishment, that is by itself.
sanskrit_cite: ādividvānmahādevastenaiṣo@dhiṣṭhito yataḥ saṃskārāstadadhiṣṭhānasiddhyai tattasya tu svataḥ

plain_english: Initiated by goddesses by that, with devotion in Shiva instruction, by firmness and distinctions he also himself from vow.
sanskrit_cite: devībhirdīkṣitastena sabhaktiḥ śivaśāsane dṛḍhatākampratābhedaiḥ so@pi svayamatha vratāt

plain_english: From teacher, austerity, mantra, and so forth, he should arrange his own purification; because it is said in Vajasineya, he should sprinkle the body himself.
sanskrit_cite: tapojapādergurutaḥ svasaṃskāraṃ prakalpayet yato vājasineyākhya uktaṃ siñcetsvayaṃ tanum

plain_english: From beginning with and so forth until end, that established; consecrated would be thus, not by external pot waters.
sanskrit_cite: ityādyupakramaṃ yāvadante tatpariniṣṭhitam abhiṣikto bhavedevaṃ na bāhyakalaśāmbubhiḥ

plain_english: Mahesha explained this in Brahmayamala and other texts; how much should be written here?
sanskrit_cite: śrīsarvavīraśrībrahmayāmalādau ca tattathā nirūpitaṃ maheśena kiyadvā likhyatāmidam

plain_english: Thus what would intuitive knowledge not accomplish for whom? From intuition all is accomplished, said the great sage Shesha.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ prātibhavijñānaṃ kiṃ kiṃ kasya na sādhayet yatprātibhādvā sarvaṃ cetyūce śeṣamahāmuniḥ

plain_english: Others say for the desireless one an intuitive teacher of such kind arises from complete means; for desired result the teacher is purified by him.
sanskrit_cite: anye tvāhurakāmasya prātibho gururīdṛśaḥ sāmagrījanyatā kāmye tenārimansaṃskṛto guruḥ

plain_english: The glory of necessity does not turn back from an achievable result; consecrated by him and practicing vow, he gives fruit.
sanskrit_cite: niyatermahimā naiva phale sādhye nivartate abhiṣiktaścīrṇavidyāvratastena phalapradaḥ

plain_english: Truth-seeing teachers say this is false, led by Somananda, Kalyana, Bhavabhuti and others.
sanskrit_cite: asadetaditi prāhurguravastattvadarśinaḥ śrīsomānandakalyāṇabhavabhūtipurogamāḥ

plain_english: For thus in the Trishika scripture exposition the wise ones said: innate knowledge is called the thought-gem.
sanskrit_cite: tathāhi trīśikāśāstravivṛtau te@bhyadhurbudhāḥ sāṃsiddhikaṃ yadvijñānaṃ taccintāratnamucyate

plain_english: In its absence that brought knowledge is honored; thus who knows in truth, for him is liberation-leading.
sanskrit_cite: tadabhāve tadarthaṃ tadāhṛtaṃ jñānamādṛtam evaṃ yo veda tattvena tasya nirvāṇagāminī

plain_english: Initiation becomes undoubted, without sesame and ghee offerings; even with unseen circle, whoever knows truth.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣā bhavatyasandigdhā tilājyāhutivarjitā adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo@pyevaṃ yaḥ kaścidvetti tattvataḥ

plain_english: He becomes always possessor of accomplishment; he is yogi and initiated; not knowing ritual or knowing ritual becomes toward sacrifice.
sanskrit_cite: sa siddhibhāgbhavennityaṃ sa yogī sa ca dīkṣitaḥ avidhijño vidhānajño jāyate yajanaṃ prati

plain_english: By such Maheshvara sentences in Trishika, knowledge and truth of initiation rites are clearly described.
sanskrit_cite: ityādibhistrīśikoktairvākyairmāheśvaraiḥ sphuṭam jñānaṃ dīkṣādisaṃskārasatattvamiti varṇitam

plain_english: The means of knowledge is initiation and rites for those lacking knowledge; this is now set aside in its own discussion.
sanskrit_cite: jñānopāyastu dīkṣādikriyā jñānaviyoginām ityetadadhunaivāstā svaprastāve bhaviṣyati

plain_english: Means of guru, scripture, authority and so on are clearly means; intuition is supreme indeed, yielding all desires, because.
sanskrit_cite: guruśāstrapramāṇāderapyupāyatvamaṃjasā pratibhā paramevaiṣā sarvakāmadughā yataḥ

plain_english: From means and yoga sequence, without means and sequence, which form is supreme truth, well established there.
sanskrit_cite: upāyayogakramato nirupāyamathākramam yadrūpaṃ tatparaṃ tattvaṃ tatra tatra suniścitam

plain_english: Who is beautiful with intuitive external and internal purification, said not serving others, therefore he is direct boon-giving teacher.
sanskrit_cite: yastu prātibhabāhyātmasaṃskāradvayasundaraḥ ukto@nanyopakāryatvātsa sākṣādvarado guruḥ

plain_english: For anyone's own liberation only, until world liberation, intuition arises like firefly, gem, star, moon, sun.
sanskrit_cite: svamuktimātre kasyāpi yāvadviśvavimocane pratibhodeti khadyotaratnatārendusūryavat

plain_english: Then for intuitive awareness this scripture made by us; whoever practices it is not indeed a teacher, for things are imitators.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ prātibhasaṃvittyai śāstramasmatkṛtaṃ tvidam yo@bhyasyetsa gururnaiva vastvarthā hi viḍambakāḥ

plain_english: With mind living on others all thus does not shine; without its statement one does not know grace descent from weakness.
sanskrit_cite: paropajīvitābuddhyā sarva itthaṃ na bhāsate taduktyā na vinā vetti śaktipātasya māndyataḥ

plain_english: This is clear and explained in those scriptures; in Kirana thus said from teacher, scripture, and self.
sanskrit_cite: sphuṭametacca śāstreṣu teṣu teṣu nirūpyate kiraṇāyāṃ tathoktaṃ ca gurutaḥ śāstrataḥ svataḥ

plain_english: Some are fit for knowledge, thus others fit for practice; in Nandishikha tantra this is expounded in detail.
sanskrit_cite: jñānayogyāstathā keciccaryāyogyāstathāpare śrīmannandiśikhātantre vitatyaitannirūpitam

plain_english: By question-answer mode that unbroken is explained; indescribable Shiva there, what means let be explained.
sanskrit_cite: praśnottaramukheneti tadabhagnaṃ nirūpyate anirdeśyaḥ śivastatra ko@bhyupāyo nirūpyatām

plain_english: Thus when question was made by goddess, glorious Shambhu explained: means here is discrimination alone, removing what is to be rejected.
sanskrit_cite: iti praśne kṛte devyā śrīmāñchaṃbhurnyarūpayam upāyo@tra vivekaikaḥ sa hi heyaṃ vihāpayan

plain_english: He gives intuitive supreme knowledge; when endowed by intuition, then liberated and liberates others.
sanskrit_cite: dadātyasya ca suśroṇi prātibhaṃ jñānamuttamam yadā pratibhayā yuktastadā muktaśca mocayet

plain_english: By descent of supreme power person's maya impurity is destroyed; prior initiation liberation now, but how from intuition?
sanskrit_cite: paraśaktinipātena dhvastamāyāmalaḥ pumān nanu prāgdīkṣayā mokṣo@dhunā tu prātibhātkatham

plain_english: Thus when question was made by goddess, lord's speech proceeded: creature is liberated by initiation and by intuition, dear one.
sanskrit_cite: iti devyā kṛte praśne prāvartata vibhorvacaḥ dīkṣayā mucyate jantuḥ prātibhena tathā priye

plain_english: Initiation depends on the guru; its intuitive nature is his own nature, which grants the isolated state.
sanskrit_cite: gurvāyattā tu sā dīkṣā badhyabandhanamokṣaṇe prātibho@sya svabhāvastu kevalībhāvasiddhidaḥ

plain_english: Liberation of the isolated one is certain by the supreme principle; the three principles are named for you.
sanskrit_cite: kevalasya dhruvaṃ muktiḥ paratattvena sā nanu nṛśaktiśivamuktaṃ hi tattvatrayamidaṃ tvayā

plain_english: Power is not bound in bondage; Shiva touches agency, and all this is stated from the guru tradition.
sanskrit_cite: nā badhyo bandhane śaktiḥ karaṇaṃ kartṛtāṃ spṛśat śivaḥ karteti tatproktaṃ sarvaṃ gurvāgamādaṇoḥ

plain_english: Again discrimination is stated; explain it further: how is discrimination, and what is discriminated, O god of gods?
sanskrit_cite: punarvivekāduktaṃ taduttarottaramucyatām kathaṃ vivekaḥ kiṃ vāsya devadeva vivicyate

plain_english: Thus spoken, the primal guru Shiva spoke the three principles from the guru tradition.
sanskrit_cite: ityukte parameśānyā jagādādiguruḥ śivaḥ śivāditattvatritayaṃ tadāgamavaśādguroḥ

plain_english: By higher words the accomplished intuitive state is attained by one cultivated through initiation.
sanskrit_cite: adhrottaragairvākyaiḥ siddhaṃ prātibhatāṃ vrajet dīkṣāsicchinnapāśatvādbhāvanābhāvitasya hi

plain_english: The principle approaches the intuitive; it is illustrated like fire covered by ashes, from the guru tradition.

sanskrit_cite: pravṛttireva prathamameṣāṃ kasmādvivicyatām karmatatsāmyavairāgyamalapākādi dūṣitam

plain_english: Lord-will is cause; and if descent-sole-causality — japa-and-the-like is action-power indeed thus, but not karma, that.
sanskrit_cite: īśvarecchā nimittaṃ cecchaktipātaikahetutā japādikā kriyāśaktirevetthaṃ natu karma tat

plain_english: Action, that world-customary indeed, giving inferior enjoyment, conceals enjoyer-form — of designation, but not our burden.
sanskrit_cite: karma tallokarūḍhaṃ hi yadbhogamavaraṃ dadat tirodhatte bhoktṛrūpaṃ saṃjñāyā tu na no bharaḥ

plain_english: Their enjoyment-excess, whence thus — if answer given: variegated-form light this, independent supreme Lord.
sanskrit_cite: teṣāṃ bhogotkatā kasmāditi ceddattamuttaram citrākāraprakāśo@yaṃ svatantraḥ parameśvaraḥ

plain_english: But from freedom, concealment-bond — in his enjoyment nourishing own enjoyer-form indeed — would be mala-karma-and-the-rest-free.
sanskrit_cite: svātantryāttu tirobhāvabandho bhoge@sya bhoktṛtām puṣṇansvaṃ rūpameva syānmalakarmādivarjitam

plain_english: Said: this Shiva's action-power, beast-dwelling, is binder — that action is called form-concealing maker.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ seyaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ śivasya paśuvartinī bandhayitrīti tatkarma kathyate rūpalopakṛt

plain_english: Known, and action-power, immediately accomplishment-furnishing — unbroken self-awareness expanse; accomplishment here is said.
sanskrit_cite: jñātā sā ca kriyāśaktiḥ sadyaḥ siddhyupapādikā avicchinnasvātmasaṃvitprathā siddhirihocyate

plain_english: She, enjoyment-liberation-freedom great-fortune, here imperishable — Vishnu-and-rest formedness in god, which, some, she by own self.
sanskrit_cite: sā bhogamokṣasvātantryamahālakṣmīrihākṣayā viṣṇvādirūpatā deve yā kācitsā nijātmanā

plain_english: By difference-yoga force, Maya-state mid-situated — thereby, by that-form-ness yoga, descent situated even, being.
sanskrit_cite: bhedayogavaśānmāyāpadamadhyavyavasthitā tena tadrūpatāyogācchaktipātaḥ sthito@pi san

plain_english: So much enjoyment lays; at end Shiva-hood, but not — as from freedom even a king favors someone.
sanskrit_cite: tāvantaṃ bhogamādhatte paryante śivatāṃ natu yathā svātantryato rājāpyanugṛhṇāti kaṃcana

plain_english: Thus from lord-power entry, Vishnu and the rest indeed — from Maya-garbha-authority descent-force, then.
sanskrit_cite: īśaśaktisamāveśāttathā viṣṇvādayo@pyalam māyāgarbhādhikārīyaśaktipātavaśāttataḥ

plain_english: Someone pradhana-purusha-discriminating, gone from nature — from excellent that, quickly indeed, someone awakened to discriminativeness.
sanskrit_cite: ko@pi pradhānapuruṣavivekī prakṛtergataḥ utkṛṣṭāttata evāśu ko@pi buddhā vivekitām

plain_english: From moment, of person, of kala — man-Maya-interval knower; of kala-abode even completely, from action turning away.
sanskrit_cite: kṣaṇātpuṃsaḥ kalāyāśca puṃmāyāntaravedakaḥ kalāśrayasyāpyatyantaṃ karmaṇo vinivartanāt

plain_english: Jnanakala, former but active, from its abode-standing — he, the supreme, at nature-root creation does not approach, ever thus.
sanskrit_cite: jñānākalaḥ prāktanastu karmī tasyāśrayasthiteḥ sa paraṃ prakṛterbudhne sṛṣṭiṃ nāyāti jātucit

plain_english: But on Maya-holders, may be created by Ananta-lord, from impulsion — vijnanakala-ness attained, from mere authority.
sanskrit_cite: māyādhare tu sṛjyetānanteśena pracodanāt vijñānākalatāṃ prāptaḥ kevalādadhikārataḥ

plain_english: From impurity, mantra-its-lords-etc. states attains always — from Shiva, from lord, from supreme — this descent indeed, from impurity.
sanskrit_cite: malānmantratadīśādibhāvameti sadā śivāt patyuḥ parasmādyastveṣa śaktipātaḥ sa vai malāt

plain_english: From named ignorance thus separated — Shiva-state revealing; not by another: Shiva-state indeed by anyone is fully revealed.
sanskrit_cite: ajñānākhyādviyokteti śivabhāvaprakāśakaḥ nānyena śivabhāvo hi kenacitsaṃprakāśate

plain_english: In Svacchanda scripture, by that said: of disputants — three hundred sixty-three exceeding, deluded, Vaishnava and the rest, at night-end.
sanskrit_cite: svacchandaśāstre tenoktaṃ vādināṃ tu śatatrayam triṣaṣṭyabhyadhikaṃ bhrāntaṃ vaiṣṇavādyaṃ niśāntare

plain_english: Shiva-knowledge alone, Shiva-ness-attainment-giving — grace-descent ending in Shiva-ness attainment is discussed.
sanskrit_cite: śivajñānaṃ kevalaṃ ca śivatāpattidāyakam śivatāpattiparyantaḥ śaktipātaśca carcyate

plain_english: Otherwise what would that be, unpresided by Shaiva power — thereby here of Vaishnava and the rest, no eligibility ever.
sanskrit_cite: anyathā kiṃ hi tatsyādyacchaivyā śaktyānadhiṣṭhitam teneha vaiṣṇavādīnāṃ nādhikāraḥ kathaṃcana

plain_english: They indeed from difference-only coursing, in nonduality far excluded — but from the great Lord's freedom, they too, if Shiva-facing.
sanskrit_cite: te hi bhedaikavṛttitvādabhede dūravarjitāḥ svātantryāttu maheśasya te@pi cecchivatonmukhāḥ

plain_english: Twofold consecration is theirs — by linga-extraction then by initiation; on bad-residue departure, with flowers the vessel is consecrated.
sanskrit_cite: dviguṇā saṃskriyāstyeṣāṃ liṅgoddhṛtyātha dīkṣayā duṣṭādhivāsavigame puṣpaiḥ kumbho@dhivāsyate

plain_english: Twofold his consecration — not thus in the pure vessel is the rule; thus this glorious grace-descent, independent, here declared.
sanskrit_cite: dviguṇo@sya sa saṃskāro netthaṃ śuddhe ghaṭe vidhiḥ itthaṃ śrīśaktipāto@yaṃ nirapekṣa ihoditaḥ

plain_english: By this very direction to be led: Matanga-raya and the rest — from text-weight fear, but having written that, not applied.
sanskrit_cite: anayaiva diśā neyaṃ mataṅgakiraṇādikam granthagauravabhītyā tu tallikhitvā na yojitam

plain_english: In Purana too, of that very, from grace devotion is accepted — by which they go to supreme accomplishment, mind-gone to his state.
sanskrit_cite: purāṇe@pi ca tasyaiva prasādādbhaktiriṣyate yayā yānti parāṃ siddhiṃ tadbhāvagatamānasāḥ

plain_english: By 'only,' action-etc. dependence is denied — grace is purification thereby, full-form-ness.
sanskrit_cite: evakāreṇa karmādisāpekṣatvaṃ niṣidhyate prasādo nirmalībhāvastena saṃpūrṇarūpatā

plain_english: By self, by that, indeed Shiva himself full shines — in Shivahood-great-accomplishment-touch-barren, but somewhere.
sanskrit_cite: ātmanā tena hi śivaḥ svayaṃ pūrṇaḥ prakāśate śivībhāvamahāsiddhisparśavandhye tu kutracit

plain_english: In Vaishnava and the rest, which devotion — not that from Shiva alone; Shiva becomes; there this is cause, but not alone.
sanskrit_cite: vaiṣṇavādau hi yā bhaktirnāsau kevalataḥ śivāt śivo bhavati tatraiṣa kāraṇaṃ na tu kevalaḥ

plain_english: Pure grace, removing dependence on limited action, leads to supreme perfection and life.
sanskrit_cite: nirmalaścāpi tu prāptāvacchitkarmādyapekṣakaḥ yayā yānti parāṃ siddhimityasyedaṃ tu jīvitam

plain_english: Even our supreme teacher Utpaladeva says the lord never deliberates when grace descends.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmānutpaladevaścāpyasmākaṃ paramo guruḥ śaktipātasamaye vicāraṇaṃ prāptamīśa na karoṣi karhicit

plain_english: Today what has come toward me? Because you delay in self-manifestation, though non-dependence on words has been declared.
sanskrit_cite: adya māṃ prati kimāgataṃ yataḥ svaprakāśanavidhau vilambase karhicitprāptaśabdābhyāmanapekṣitvamūcivān

plain_english: Rarity and non-attachment in the lord's grace descent reveal the variegation of that very grace by half-measures.
sanskrit_cite: durlabhatvamarāgitvaṃ śaktipātavidhau vibhoḥ aparārdhena tasyaiva śaktipātasya citratām

plain_english: The glorious unobstructed one describes the lord's awakening power through delays, long and short differences, and so on.
sanskrit_cite: vyavadhānacirakṣiprabhedādyairupavarṇitaiḥ śrīmatāpyaniruddhena śaktimunmīlinīṃ vibhoḥ

plain_english: In the Matanga, independence is described as the god's own-form unfolding, even at the end of immovable beings.
sanskrit_cite: vyācakṣāṇena mātaṅge varṇitā nirapekṣatā sthāvarānte@pi devasya svarūponmīlanātmikā

plain_english: Descending power is never dependent anywhere; thus, even when this varied grace descent is established, it remains so.
sanskrit_cite: śaktiḥ patantī sāpekṣā na kvāpīti suvistarāt evaṃ vicitre@pyetasmiñchaktipāte sthite sati

plain_english: By gradation differences and so on, variegation among initiates arises; some attain a rudra-hundred measure through that grace.
sanskrit_cite: tāratamyādibhirbhedaiḥ samayyādivicitratā kaścidrudrāśatāmātrāpādanāttatprasādataḥ

plain_english: An initiate may gradually attain shivahood; some pure-path-bound son attains it quickly and without sequence.
sanskrit_cite: śivatvaṃ kramaśo gacchet samayī yo nirūpyate kaścicchuddhādhvabandhaḥ san putrakaḥ śīghramakramāt

plain_english: By an enjoyment obstacle, some practitioner is slow or quick; some is fully obligated in a share of the five acts.
sanskrit_cite: bhogavyavadhinā ko@pi sādhakaściraśīghrataḥ kaścitsaṃpūrṇakartavyaḥ kṛtyapañcakabhāgini

plain_english: The teacher standing in form also bears enjoyment, liberation, and other differences for the fourfold initiate, by summary and expansion.
sanskrit_cite: rūpe sthito guruḥ so@pi bhogamokṣādibhedabhāk samayyādicatuṣkasya samāsavyāsayogataḥ

plain_english: By gradual, immediate, and other differences, grace descent is variegated; gradual grace descent is in Siddhanta and Vama, then.
sanskrit_cite: kramākramādibhirbhedaiḥ śaktipātasya citratā kramikaḥ śaktipātaśca siddhānte vāmake tataḥ

plain_english: In Daksha, Mata, Kula, Kaula, half-of-six, and heart, then, or by transcending power, suddenly and without sequence, or.
sanskrit_cite: dakṣe mate kule kaule ṣaḍardhe hṛdaye tataḥ ullaṅghanavaśādvāpi jhaṭityakramameva vā

plain_english: It is said in the glorious Bhairava Kula: the teacher, well-prepared by five initiations and transcending the lower stream, indeed follows Trika scripture.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ śrībhairavakule pañcadīkṣāsusaṃskṛtaḥ gururullaṅghitādhaḥsthasrotā vai trikaśāstragaḥ

plain_english: By knowledge, conduct, and other differences, indeed superiority and inferiority arise; the lord is in such glorious scriptures of all conduct, heart, and so on.
sanskrit_cite: jñānācārādibhedena hyuttarādharatā vibhuḥ śāstreṣvadīdṛśacchrīmatsarvācārahṛdādiṣu

plain_english: Even a teacher anointed in the left path and knowing the supreme principle still deserves purification again in the Bhairava tantra.
sanskrit_cite: vāmamārgābhiṣiktastu daiśikaḥ paratattvavit tathāpi bhairave tantre punaḥ saṃskāramarhati

plain_english: Shaiva, Vaimala, Siddhanta, Arhats, and artisans—all are to be known as bound souls in Bhairava's mother circle.
sanskrit_cite: śaivavaimalasiddhāntā ārhatāḥ kārukāśca ye sarve te paśavo jñeyā bhairave mātṛmaṇḍale

plain_english: In Kula Kali procedure it is indeed said: especially Vaishnavas, and those devoted to ash and so on, have no fitness.
sanskrit_cite: kulakālīvidhau coktaṃ vaiṣṇavānā viśeṣataḥ bhasmaniṣṭhāprapannānāmityādau naiva yogyatā

plain_english: In the Svacchanda scripture, glorious Mahesha said briefly: one devoted to other scripture is not a giver of accomplishment fruit.
sanskrit_cite: svacchandaśāstre saṃkṣepāduktaṃ ca śrīmaheśinā anyaśāstrarato yastu nāsau siddhiphalapradaḥ

plain_english: Indeed a teacher is considered one who obtained anointment by initiate sequence; and what connection is there, thus by power, among Vaishnavas and others?
sanskrit_cite: samayyādikramāllabdhābhiṣeko hi gururmataḥ sa ca śaktivaśāditthaṃ vaiṣṇavādiṣu ko@nvayaḥ

plain_english: By deceit, false hearing, and so on, one taking that knowledge may incur penance; thus what qualification may be here?
sanskrit_cite: chadmāpaśravaṇādyaistu tajjñānaṃ gṛhṇato bhavet prāyaścittamatastādṛgadhikāryatra kiṃ bhavet

plain_english: A disciple endowed with desire for fruit, whose accomplishment depends on that, would certainly be cooked in hell by resorting to penance.
sanskrit_cite: phalākāṅkṣāyutaḥ śiṣyastadekāyattasiddhikaḥ dhruvaṃ pacyeta narake prāyaścittyupasevanāt

plain_english: This concealment mode, appointed in such a teacher by Shiva, with devotion to him, is not called his grace descent.
sanskrit_cite: tirobhāvaprakāro@yaṃ yattādṛśi niyojitaḥ gurau śivena tadbhaktiḥ śaktipāto@sya nocyate

plain_english: When by variety force one knows his such reversed conduct state, knowledge, therefore one should remove it.
sanskrit_cite: yadātu vaicitryavaśājjānīyāttasya tādṛśam viparītapravṛttatvaṃ jñānaṃ tasmādupāharet

plain_english: One should abandon sinful conduct and become devoted to knowledge, just as a king seizes wealth taken from a thief.
sanskrit_cite: taṃ ca tyajetpāpavṛttiṃ bhavettu jñānatatparaḥ yathā caurādgṛhītvārthaṃ taṃ nigṛhṇāti bhūpatiḥ

plain_english: Likewise, from Vaishnava and other sources, the right-minded one takes Shaiva knowledge; even when heard, a single mode of difference remains in Shiva-knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: vaiṣṇavādestathā śaivaṃ jñānamāhṛtya sanmatiḥ sa hi bhedaikavṛttitvaṃ śivajñāne śrute@pyalam

plain_english: It is said he does not abandon firmly; the best bound soul stationed in Vama is concealed and placed by Shiva alone, by force of order.
sanskrit_cite: nojjhatīti dṛḍhaṃ vāmādhiṣṭhitastatpaśūttamaḥ śivenaiva tirobhāvya sthāpito niyaterbalāt

plain_english: How should the dependent one proceed step by step? The scripture of free will says this, and it addresses those devoted among Vaishnavas and others.
sanskrit_cite: kathaṅkāraṃ patipadaṃ prayātu paratantritaḥ svacchandaśāstre proktaṃ ca vaiṣṇavādiṣu ye ratāḥ

plain_english: Maya indeed deludes them in non-liberation, by desire for liberation; Vaishnava and others join Shaiva scripture to their own teaching.
sanskrit_cite: bhramayatyeva tānmāyā hyamokṣe mokṣalipsayā vaiṣṇavādiḥ śaivaśāstraṃ melayannijaśāsane

plain_english: Certainly, one who has fallen into doubt may go to loss of both, in his own view and in the other's view, from transgressing agreement.
sanskrit_cite: dhruvaṃ saṃśayamāpanna ubhayabhraṣṭatāṃ vrajet svadṛṣṭau paradṛṣṭau ca samayollaṅghanādasau

plain_english: Because harm approaches, one should practice such a course; it was said by the supreme lord in glorious Gahvara.
sanskrit_cite: pratyavāyaṃ yato@bhyeti carettannedṛśaṃ kramam uktaṃ śrīmadgahvare ca parameśena tādṛśam

plain_english: Shiva-knowledge does not shine among those engaged in other scriptures; the Siddhantin is not in the left, nor is he in the right, in our opinion.
sanskrit_cite: nānyaśāstrābhiyuktaṣu śivajñānaṃ prakāśate tanna saiddhāntiko vāme nāsau dakṣe sa no mate

plain_english: He is not the former in Kula, Kaula, or Trika; elsewhere he is bounded or unbounded, and does not know infinity situated.
sanskrit_cite: kulakaule trike nāsau pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ paratra tu avacchinno@navacchedaṃ no vettyānantyasaṃsthitaḥ

plain_english: The all-enduring one is below, the authorized one is above; the teacher enlivens lower actions by touching the lower.
sanskrit_cite: sarvaṃsahastato@dhaḥstha ūrdhvastho@dhikṛto guruḥ svātmīyādharasaṃsparśātprāṇayannadharāḥ kriyāḥ

plain_english: The supreme teacher makes fruitful that which is above; even one below, seeing such, serving the teacher, may become he.
sanskrit_cite: saphalīkurute yattadūrdhvastho gururuttamaḥ adhaḥsthadṛkstho@pyetādṛggurusevī bhavetsa yaḥ

plain_english: One kindled by such descent of power may quickly lead this upward, in a field-seat bounded like a mountain-river.
sanskrit_cite: tādṛkśaktinipāteddho yo drāgūrdhvamimaṃ nayet tattadgirinadīprāyāvacchinne kṣetrapīṭhake

plain_english: Even with ever-higher knowledge, one who is a lower bearer does not become qualified; one must seek a progressively higher teacher.
sanskrit_cite: uttarottaravijñāne nādhikāryadharo@dharaḥ uttarottaramācāryaṃ vidannapyadharo@dharaḥ

plain_english: One who performs unqualified action and transgresses scripture becomes punishable; by grace-power alone there is varied fitness for knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: kurvannadhikriyāṃ śāstralaṅghī nigrahabhājanam śaktipātabalādeva jñānayogyavicitratā

plain_english: Scriptural, thought-born, and meditation-born knowledge exist, but meditation-born knowledge beyond them is greater because it alone is the cause of liberation.
sanskrit_cite: śrautaṃ cintāmayaṃ dvyātma bhāvanāmayameva ca jñānaṃ taduttaraṃ jyāyo yato mokṣaikakāraṇam

plain_english: How could one extract from principles or make connection at any time without supreme meditation-born knowledge?
sanskrit_cite: tattvebhya uddhṛtiṃ kvāpi yojanaṃ sakale@kale kathaṃ kuryādvinā jñānaṃ bhāvanāmayamuttamam

plain_english: Even a yogi who has attained perfection in principles up to the highest place beginning with Sadashiva becomes a connector only through habituated knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: yogī tu prāptatattattvasiddhirapyuttame pade sadāśivādye svabhyastajñānitvādeva yojakaḥ

plain_english: Even firm perfection born of yoga in lower principles is not a means for liberation, like a wealth-tree.
sanskrit_cite: adhareṣu ca tattveṣu yā siddhiryogajāsya sā vimocanāyāṃ nopāyaḥ sthitāpi dhanadāravat

plain_english: He who has arisen with perfection of all paths is indeed Sadashiva; how would this directly present one liberate mortals while going?
sanskrit_cite: yastūtpannasamastādhvasiddhiḥ sahi sadāśivaḥ sākṣādeṣa kathaṃ martyānmocayedgurutāṃ vrajan

plain_english: As said in the Malini Tantra, considering one joined with knowledge, the wise declare the possessor of habituated knowledge to be liberating.
sanskrit_cite: tenoktaṃ mālinītantre vicārya jñānayogite yataśca mokṣadaḥ proktaḥ svabhyastajñānavānbudhaiḥ

plain_english: Therefore habituated knowledge alone is the one mark of a guru; this distinction, declared by me, is shown by Shambhunatha.
sanskrit_cite: tasmātsvabhyastavijñānataivaikaṃ gurulakṣaṇam vibhāgastveṣa me proktaḥ śaṃbhunāthena darśyate

plain_english: One intent on liberation-knowledge should make the habituated knower guru and abandon even an already obtained other; thus it was said by Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: mokṣajñānaparaḥ kuryādguruṃ svabhyastavedanam anyaṃ tyajetprāptamapi tathācoktaṃ śivena tat

plain_english: As a bee seeking fragrance goes from flower to flower, so a disciple seeking knowledge may go from guru to another guru.
sanskrit_cite: āmodārthī yathā bhṛṅgaḥ puṣpātpuṣpāntaraṃ vrajet vijñānārthī tathā śiṣyo gurorgurvantaraṃ vrajet

plain_english: Having obtained a powerless guru, how could one rely on him for liberation-knowledge, O goddess? From a tree with destroyed root, whence flowers and fruits?
sanskrit_cite: śaktihīnaṃ guruṃ prāpya mokṣajñāne kathaṃ śrayet naṣṭamūle drume devi kutaḥ puṣpaphalādikam

plain_english: Seeing higher-and-higher excellence-fortune, yet situated in the lowest — who in place? Therefore who else would be fate-burnt?
sanskrit_cite: uttarottaramutkarṣalakṣmīṃ paśyannapi sthitaḥ adhame yaḥ pade tasmātko@nyaḥ syāddaivadagdhakaḥ

plain_english: But who enjoyment and liberation and desires knowledge only — self-practiced knower, yoga-accomplished: he should resort to guru.
sanskrit_cite: yastu bhogaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca vāñchedvijñānameva ca svabhyastajñāninaṃ yogasiddhaṃ sa gurumāśrayet

plain_english: In that absence, resort to the knowledge-liberation knower — in enjoyment-share, the yogin who would be able to give that fruit.
sanskrit_cite: tadabhāve tu vijñānamokṣayorjñāninaṃ śrayet bhuktyaṃśe yoginaṃ yastatphalaṃ dātuṃ bhavetkṣamaḥ

plain_english: In fruit-giving-incapable, danger-only-teaching yogin — better the knower who shows means and would liberate.
sanskrit_cite: phaladānākṣame yoginyapāyaikopadeśini varaṃ jñānī yo@bhyupāyaṃ diśedapica mocayet

plain_english: Knower, not full, just one — if by part-of-part order, having taken knowledges, would make discernment, unbroken circle.
sanskrit_cite: jñānī na pūrṇa evaiko yadi hyaṃśāṃśikākramāt jñānānyādāya vijñānaṃ kurvītākhaṇḍamaṇḍalam

plain_english: Thereby countless gurus make, for filling own awareness — but blessed: full discernment the knowledge-seeker obtains guru.
sanskrit_cite: tenāsaṃkhyāngurūnkuryātpūraṇāya svasaṃvidaḥ dhanyastu pūrṇavijñānaṃ jñānārthī labhate gurum

plain_english: Various guru-tradition-stream intuition-only mixed, having made the knowledge-ocean — by own drops would flood, or what?
sanskrit_cite: nānāgurvāgamasrotaḥpratibhāmātramiśritam kṛtvā jñānārṇavaṃ svābhirvipruṅgiḥ plāvayenna kim

plain_english: Up to Tapana-to-Motaka-end, whose is my guru-sequence — his, my, of all disciples, no teaching-poverty.
sanskrit_cite: ā tapanānmoṭakāntaṃ yasya me@sti gurukramaḥ tasya me sarvaśiṣyasya nopadeśadaridratā

plain_english: By glorious Kallata thus, by guru described — I too therefore, from lower-scripture-view curiosity.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmatā kallaṭenetthaṃ guruṇā tu nyarūpyata ahamapyata evādhaḥśāstradṛṣṭikutūhalāt

plain_english: Logicians vedists buddhists jains vishnu-followers I did not serve — from world-soul-beyond-path karma-yoga ordination.
sanskrit_cite: tārkikaśrautabauddhārhadvaiṣṇavādīnnaseviṣi lokādhyātmātimārgādikarmayogavidhānataḥ

plain_english: From awakening-excess abundance, contemplate the gradually excellent — in former scripture, questioners: sages Narada and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: saṃbodhotkarṣabāhulyātkramotkṛṣṭānvibhāvayet śrīpūrvaśāstre praṣṭāro munayo nāradādayaḥ

plain_english: Former Vishnu-followers and buddhists, knowing siddhanta and the rest thence — gradually trika-meaning knowledge-moon eager-sighted.
sanskrit_cite: prāgvaiṣṇavāḥ saugatāśca siddhāntādividastataḥ kramāttrikārthavijñānacandrotsukitadṛṣṭayaḥ

plain_english: Therefore never doubt guru-multitude — in another-guru-delighting fool, in other-agama serving.
sanskrit_cite: tasmānna gurubhūyastve viśaṅketa kadācana gurvantararate mūḍhe āgamāntarasevake

plain_english: Falling-away which is declared, that thus let be understood — who, where, in treatise authorized, he there is called guru.
sanskrit_cite: pratyavāyo ya āmnātaḥ sa itthamiti gṛhyatām yo yatra śāstre@dhikṛtaḥ sa tatra gururucyate

plain_english: There unauthorized, but who, is called that other guru — as seated in that circle toward the other-circle king.
sanskrit_cite: tatrānadhikṛto yastu tadgurvantaramucyate yathā tanmaṇḍalāsīno maṇḍalāntarabhūpatim

plain_english: Own-circle desiring to conquer, fully serving, perishes — so higher-higher knowledge-siddhi desiring, resorting.
sanskrit_cite: svamaṇḍalajigīṣuḥ sansevamāno vinaśyati tathottarottarajñānasiddhiprepsuḥ samāśrayan

plain_english: Lower-than-lower teacher goes to destruction — so indeed higher-abiding, from agama, siddhi-desiring.
sanskrit_cite: adharādharamācāryaṃ vināśamadhigacchati evamevordhvavartiṣṇorāgamātsiddhivāñchakaḥ

plain_english: Maya-scripture devoted attains destruction — and said in glorious Bliss: action, having resorted, from being.
sanskrit_cite: māyīyaśāstranirato vināśaṃ pratipadyate uktaṃ ca śrīmadānande karma saṃśritya bhāvataḥ

plain_english: Despises that, and in that resorts elsewhere to the fruitless — day by day decreasing thus, is cooked in Raurava and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: jugupsate tattasmiṃśca viphale@nyatsamāśrayet dināddinaṃ hrasaṃstvevaṃ pacyate rauravādiṣu

plain_english: Who upward-path seeking, lower guru-agama abandoned by descent — he blessed, made forward-facing.
sanskrit_cite: yastūrdhvordhvapathaprepsuradharaṃ gurumāgamam jihāsecchaktipātena sa dhanyaḥ pronmukhīkṛtaḥ

plain_english: Therefore indeed here, in scriptures, in Shaiva only is determined — toward other-scripture-meanings despairing, the purifying rule.
sanskrit_cite: ata eveha śāstreṣu śaiveṣveva nirūpyate śāstrāntarārthānāśvastānprati saṃskārako vidhiḥ

plain_english: Therefore also supreme Shaiva — who elsewhere fallen, he indeed here to be graced; upward and upward, but of the guide, fallen sometimes.
sanskrit_cite: ataścāpyuttamaṃ śaivaṃ yo@nyatra patitaḥ sahi ihānugrāhya ūrdhvordhvaṃ netastu patitaḥ kvacit

plain_english: Therefore indeed, for by omniscient Brahma-Vishnu-and-the-rest in own teaching, not handed down — linga-uprooting and the rest, anything.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva hi sarvajñairbrahmaviṣṇvādibhirnije na śāsane samāmnātaṃ liṅgoddhārādi kiṃcana

plain_english: Thus Vishnu-and-the-rest, Shaiva-ultimate-sole knowers — toward some, so initiated; from delusion, dissent resorted.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ viṣṇvādayaḥ śaivaparamārthaikavedinaḥ kāṃścitprati tathādikṣuste mohādvimatiṃ śritāḥ

plain_english: Seeing such a mind incapable of touching truth among these, even buddhas like Brahma and Vishnu speak thus; therefore this śaktipāta is distinguished by reasoning and scripture.
sanskrit_cite: tathāvidhāmeva matiṃ satyasaṃsparśanākṣamām dṛṣṭvaiṣāṃ brahmaviṣṇvādyairbuddhairapi tathoditam

plain_english: Thus this śaktipāta is distinguished by reasoning and scripture.
sanskrit_cite: ityeṣa yuktyāgamataḥ śaktipāto vivecitaḥ
